description: Changes the chart the signed-in member has open right now in Vela, in their browser: the market (symbol), the timeframe, the chart type, the trading session, the price scale, the dates on screen, and the multi-chart layout. Send only what should change; everything else on the chart stays, and it never adds or removes an indicator or a drawing (vela_add_indicator and vela_remove_indicators do the first). Use it when the member asks to switch their own chart ("put ETH on my chart", "go to the 15 minute", "split it in four"), and before vela_mark_up_chart when the analysis they ask for is of another market or timeframe. The member sees the change happen and is told an assistant made it. Returns what the chart shows afterwards, in words, with no prices: check the market it names is the one asked for. A custom timeframe or a CME futures market the member's plan does not include changes nothing and says which plan limit it is. To show or change a chart inside the chat instead, use chart_open and chart_command. With the member's Vela tab on screen it happens in front of them within seconds. When it is not (they are in another tab), the change is queued and applied the moment they look at Vela again, within 10 minutes: the result then says queued, so tell them to open Vela. Requires signing in with a LuxAlgo account (OAuth).

charts.description: Changes per chart, each for one chart of the layout (by slot) or for the chart the member is working on.

chart_type.description: How the price is drawn. "footprint" and "tpo" are the orderflow charts, built from real trades: crypto, US stocks and ETFs and CME futures, not forex or commodities.

scale.description: Price scale settings; send only the ones that change.

mode.description: "price" is the plain price scale, "percent" the change in percent, "indexed" indexed to 100.

session.description: Trading session, where the market has one (US stocks and futures); ignored elsewhere.

slot.description: One chart of a multi-chart layout, by position (0 is the top-left, in reading order). Leave it out for the chart the member is working on.

symbol.description: The market. Prefer the bare ticker, which Vela resolves across every venue it serves: "AAPL", "SPY", "EURUSD", "XAUUSD" (gold), "BTCUSDT". To pin a venue use PREFIX:TICKER with one of Vela's sources only: BINANCE ("BTCUSDT", perpetuals "BTCUSDT.P"), BINANCE.US, COINBASE (dash form, "BTC-USD"), HYPERLIQUID (the base asset only, "BTC"), BYBIT, NASDAQ / NYSE / AMEX / BATS (US stocks and ETFs, "NASDAQ:AAPL"), FX ("EURUSD"), COMMODITIES ("XAUUSD"), CME (futures, always with the prefix: "CME:ES1!"). The ticker must be in that venue's own form, and venue prefixes from other charting platforms (OANDA, TVC, FX_IDC) are not read: the result says what the chart shows afterwards, so check it took.

timeframe.description: Any amount from 1 minute up: minutes ("1", "15", "22m"), hours ("1h", "4h"), days ("D", "3D"), weeks ("W", "2W") or months ("M"). Lowercase m is minutes, uppercase M is months; a bare number is minutes. There are no seconds or tick timeframes.

visible_range.description: The dates on screen: a preset, or from and to together.

from.description: Start of an exact window, ISO 8601 date or date and time.

to.description: End of an exact window, ISO 8601.

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

layout.description: Multi-chart layout: "1" one chart, "2h" two side by side, "2v" two stacked, "4" (2 by 2), "8" (2 by 4), "g<rows>x<cols>" up to 4 each (e.g. "g3x3"), or one big chart with smaller ones: "big-left-2", "big-left-3", "big-right-2", "big-top-2", "big-top-3", "big-bottom-2". A smaller layout closes the charts that no longer fit.

name: vela_set_chart
title: Change my open Vela chart
